title: Add Support for Custom Prompts Folder and Selector in UI
body:
Hi,

I'd love to see a feature that lets users create a folder for custom prompts in the current working directory. These prompts should be in Markdown format (.md) and selectable via a dropdown in the UI.

**Key Features:**
- **Custom Prompts Folder:** Let users store prompts in a specific directory.
- **UI Selector:** Add a dropdown to switch between these prompts.
- **Variable Support:** Allow using variables like `{{TASK}}` in the prompts. For each `{{VAR}}`, create an input field in the UI.

**Use Case:**
This would make it super easy to switch between different prompts for various tasks or projects. For instance, someone working on multiple projects can have specific prompts for each and switch between them easily. The variable support would allow users to dynamically adjust prompt content based on their needs.

**Example:**
- **Folder Structure:**
  ```
  ./prompts
  ├── readme_prompt.md
  ├── doc_prompt.md
  └── general_prompt.md
  ```

- **Prompt File Content:**
  ```markdown
  Before proceeding with the request, read the following documents:
  - [README.md](./README.md)
  - [Documentation](./docs)
  
  Task: {{TASK}}
  ```

- **UI Implementation:**
  When selecting a prompt with `{{TASK}}`, an input field labeled "TASK" appears in the UI to enter the specific task dynamically.

**Benefits:**
- **Customization:** Create tailored prompts for different tasks.
- **Efficiency:** Switch between prompts quickly without manual changes.
- **Flexibility:** Use variables like `{{TASK}}` to dynamically change prompt content.

Thanks for considering this feature!

title: Add web search tool to get latest docs for dependencies
body:
When working on a Ruby project for example, you’ll have a Gemfile that lists the libraries for your current project, and you may want to add new gems as well for adding certain functionality.

Ideally, Claude Dev is aware of the current docs for any given library in a project, and either the full docs or the relevant sections of the docs are included in any prompts generated for a user’s requested change.

Do you have a recommended way to make this work well? 

I actually used Claude Dev last night to build a script that accepts a Ruby gem name and generates a single markdown file containing the Readme of the gem, table of contents for all classes and methods, and then all of the RDOC docs for the methods in the gemfile (I took some inspiration from the mutable.ai wiki approach, albeit in a basic initial form. I think these could be even more powerful by using LLMs to generate method descriptions for any weak or missing RDOCs, but not there yet).

Does it make sense to create a /docs folder in my project and put all of these markdown files in it? Is there a way to make sure Claude Dev is aware of those? Or would this be a good feature addition?

My perfect end state would be all gems in my Gemfile automatically get their docs synced to the project I’m working on for Claude Dev to leverage, and even better would also be a way for Claude Dev to discover gems it could use to implement a given feature request, perhaps from an API that accepts a query for use case/functionality and returns a list of gems that could be useful for that.

What do you think?

title: Feature Request: Implement Context Management and Message Editing for Improved LLM Performance
body:
## Background
When implementing a feature, I've noticed that as I get deeper into the task, the LLM starts to struggle with solving issues. Each iteration doesn't necessarily contribute to solving the problem, as the growing context seems to impair its problem-solving abilities.

## Observations
- Starting a new task, even without the full context of the previous work, often results in higher quality problem-solving and better handling of errors and sub-tasks.
- The base message sent with every request grows larger over time, potentially polluting the context.

## Proposed Solutions

### 1. Context Management
Implement a system to manage the context of tasks. This could include:
- Displaying information about how many tokens are already used up for chat history (maybe the cached prompts would be the size of this?). There could be an indicator with green, yellow and red, so users can quickly see if they're reaching the maximum possible tokens per request. 
- Allowing users to start from an earlier state when beginning a new task.

### 2. Message Editing
Add the ability to edit previously sent messages that didn't result in a satisfactory response from the LLM. This could significantly improve efficiency in using the tool.

### 3. Context Addition Optimization
Investigate and potentially optimize how information is added to the context. The exact logic behind this process I haven't investigated, but there may be room for improvement.

## Benefits
- These changes would help users strategically finish tasks before hitting the 200,000 token limit (related to issue #106).
- Improved LLM performance by maintaining a more relevant and focused context.
- Enhanced user control over the conversation flow and context.

## Next Steps
- [ ] Research current context management implementation
- [ ] Design UI for displaying token usage and context management options
- [ ] Implement prototype of message editing feature
- [ ] Investigate optimization possibilities for context addition logic
- [ ] User testing and feedback collection

## Related Issues
- #106 (regarding the 200,000 token limit)

# Claude Dev Plugin Issue Summary

## Environment
- Claude Dev plugin for VS Code
- Running on a Chromebook

## Problem
Terminal output is visible to the user but not relayed to the AI assistant (Claude).

This happened after some significant repo restructures that came with various errors, changes to gitignore, and other configuration updates, so something may have gone off during that process.

## Impact
The AI assistant cannot see the results of executed commands or any terminal output, limiting its ability to assist with debugging and development tasks.

## Recommendations for Users
1. Reinstall the Claude Dev plugin for VS Code.
2. If the issue persists after reinstallation, submit a bug report to the plugin developers using this summary.
3. As a workaround, manually copy and paste relevant terminal output into the conversation when needed.

## Recommendations for Plugin Developers
1. Investigate the output capture and relay mechanism in the Claude Dev plugin, specifically for Chromebook environments.
2. Ensure that the plugin has the necessary permissions to access and relay terminal output.
3. Implement logging or diagnostics within the plugin to help identify where the output relay is failing.
4. Consider adding a configuration option for users to toggle verbose logging, which could help in troubleshooting similar issues.

## Next Steps
1. Submit a detailed bug report to the plugin developers using this updated summary.
2. Continue to use the workaround of manually providing terminal output when necessary.
3. Monitor for any updates or patches to the Claude Dev plugin that might address this issue.

## Recent Actions Taken
1. Uninstalled the Claude Dev plugin for VS Code.
2. Reloaded VS Code.
3. Reinstalled the Claude Dev plugin for VS Code.
4. Performed a full system reboot.
5. Tested the plugin after the reboot by running simple commands (e.g., 'echo' and 'ls -la').

## Current Status After Reboot
The issue persists even after a full system reboot. The AI assistant (Claude) is still unable to see the output from terminal commands, although the user can see the output in their terminal.

## Next Steps for Bug Report
1. Provide a detailed description of the environment: OS version, VS Code version, Claude Dev plugin version.

   b. Attempt to run a simple command (e.g., 'echo "Hello"' or 'ls -la')

3. Include any relevant log files or error messages if available.
4. Mention that the issue persists after reinstallation and system reboot.

title: Shell Integration disruption after running pre-commit hook
body:
# Claude Dev Plugin: Terminal Output Reading Issue

## Issue Description

The Claude Dev plugin lost the ability to read terminal output across different environments (local and GitHub Codespaces) after executing a pre-commit hook that runs a project summarization script. This issue persists even in new, clean branches and fresh Codespaces.

## Key Observations

1. The issue is specific to the Claude Dev plugin; terminal output is still visible to the user.
2. The problem occurs in both local and GitHub Codespaces environments.
3. The issue was triggered after running a pre-commit hook that executes a Python script.
4. The problem persists across different sessions, branches, and newly created Codespaces.
5. Pylance is the only other VS Code extension installed.
6. A similar script in a different repository (express.js), also created by Claude, led to the same behavior in that development environment.

## Triggering Script Details

The pre-commit hook that triggered the issue contains the following code:

```sh
#!/bin/sh

# Run the Python script to summarize the project
python3 /workspaces/credex-bot/summarize_project.py

# Add the generated summary to the commit
git add /workspaces/credex-bot/docs/code_summary.md

# Continue with the commit
exit 0
```

This hook runs a Python script (`summarize_project.py`) to generate a project summary and adds it to the commit.

## Potential Causes

The issue likely stems from an internal bug in the Claude Dev plugin, possibly related to:

1. Output buffering issues when executing external scripts
2. Asynchronous processing problems with Git hooks
3. State management errors after script execution
4. Permission or security feature mishandling during Git operations
5. Memory management issues triggered by the summarization process
6. Interaction problems with Codespaces' terminal emulation during hook execution
7. Version-specific bug related to handling Git hook outputs

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up a Git repository with the above pre-commit hook.
2. Create or modify a file to trigger a commit.
3. Attempt to commit the changes, which will execute the pre-commit hook.
4. After the commit process, try to use the Claude Dev plugin to read any terminal output.
5. Observe that the plugin cannot read the output, while it remains visible in the terminal.

## Environment Details

- VS Code Version: codespaces
- Claude Dev Plugin Version: latest
- Operating System: codespaces
- GitHub Codespaces: not sure

## Additional Context

- The issue persists even after creating new Codespaces and branches, suggesting it might be related to account-level settings or a fundamental interaction between the plugin and Codespaces.
- A similar issue was observed in a JavaScript project on a local machine with a comparable script, indicating the problem might not be limited to a specific programming language or environment.
- The problem seems to be reproducible across different projects when similar summarization scripts are used in pre-commit hooks.


## Impact

This issue significantly impairs the functionality of the Claude Dev plugin, as it can no longer read terminal output after the hook execution. This limitation severely affects the plugin's usefulness in development workflows, especially in projects utilizing Git hooks for automated tasks.

## Description
When executing commands through Shell Integration, Claude Dev occasionally fails to retrieve the command output.

## Steps to Reproduce
Note: The reproduction rate is variable and environment-dependent. In my environment (described below), the issue occurred approximately 6 out of 10 times.

1. Execute the following prompt: "Run `date` and display the output. If the output is empty, just say 'Empty'."
2. When Claude Dev requests permission to execute the command, click the "Run Command" button.
3. After a brief wait, Claude Dev may respond with "Empty" instead of the command output.

To increase the likelihood of reproduction, you may need to instruct Claude Dev to try "Again" multiple times. A video demonstrating 10 attempts in my environment can be viewed here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GXnYe3Trr_c

## Expected Behavior
Claude Dev should consistently read and report the command execution results.

## Environment
- VS Code Version: 1.93.1
- Shell: zsh 5.9 (aarch64-apple-darwin23.5.0)
- OS: macOS 14.5 (23F79)
- Claude Dev: main (3a850b029934b3844edffd32e60cc7d3f97b5d99)

## Investigation Findings

While not conclusive, the issue appears to be related to the `read()` method of VSCode's Shell Integration API.

The `read()` method returns an AsyncIterable<string>, but the data extracted from it is inconsistent even when executing the same command repeatedly. To observe this, I added console.log statements to the run method of the TerminalProcess class in Claude Dev:

         // todo: need to handle errors

+            console.log({ data })
```

```

Entries marked with ★ indicate successful capture of the command output by Claude Dev.

The VS Code TERMINAL tab shows that commands are executed correctly:

title: Feature Request: Enable Multi-LLM Workflow with Smart Routing Mechanism
body:
Currently, the Claude Dev extension uses a single LLM to handle all coding tasks at any given time. I would like to propose a feature that enables a multiple LLM workflow, where more capable models can assign specific tasks to other specialized models based on their strengths. This smart routing mechanism would allow the extension to utilize the best-suited models for different coding-related tasks, optimizing the overall process.

Feature Requirements:

1. Smart LLM Routing:
Implement a system where a more capable model (e.g., Claude or GPT-4) acts as a "manager" to route tasks to other LLMs that excel in specific areas (e.g., Copilot for autocompletion, Codex for code generation, etc.).

2. LLM Task Assignment:
The "manager" LLM should be able to break down complex coding problems into smaller subtasks and delegate them to specialized LLMs that are efficient at specific tasks (e.g., debugging, refactoring, documentation, etc.).

3. Customizable LLM Integration:
Allow users to integrate different LLMs based on their use case, choosing from a list of supported models, and configure routing rules based on model strengths.

4. Model Communication Protocol:
Implement a communication layer where LLMs can interact, share context, and collaborate on code-related tasks. The "manager" LLM should maintain the overall context while task-specific LLMs handle subtasks.

5. Improved Task Efficiency:
The smart routing mechanism should aim to increase efficiency by delegating specific parts of the workflow to models that can handle them faster and more accurately than a single LLM would.

title: Claude Dev suggested changes.
body:
Issues with Claude Dev that I feel need to be addressed for it to become truly useful in developing code:

There absolutely needs to be a way to stop it's response.  If Claude goes off with an incorrect understanding of the task, it cannot be stopped without loosing the current context.  This leads to a LOT of wasted time.  If the user rejects a change, Claude-Dev needs to stop and find out why instead of just going on its merry way.   Otherwise you just keep wracking up costs for no reason.  Every time you have to kill a conversation, you burn a lot of money.  I have tried many ways to work this into queries, but the way it works under the hood prevents Claude from following instructions asking it to ask for continuation permission after a file update.

Continuing that thought, some sort of automated summary of the current chat that can be used to prime the next  one would be fantastic.

Next is a recurring problem.  Claude likes to return these sorts of shortcuts: # ... (previous functions remain unchanged) which ends up deleting chunks of code you don't want deleted.  These types of responses either need to be automatically rebuffed by Claude-Dev, or the review process should be better at applying random block changes to the code.

I know this is called Claude-Dev for a reason, but limiting your choices to just Claude adds needless  expense when you are doing something within the capabilities of much cheaper models.  There needs to be some way to use other models.  right now, when I try I just get a lot of errors where Claude-Dev tries to use advanced Claude features and fails.  This is a large step backward.

🚀 Feature Proposal for Cline: Multi-API Switch Module
Problem
Currently, Cline users often rely on single API configurations, which makes workflows rigid and challenging to adapt to changing requirements. This limitation reduces the flexibility to switch between APIs dynamically for tasks like NLP, image recognition, or various automation tools.

Solution
The Multi-API Switch Module would allow Cline users to switch between APIs on-the-fly based on defined conditions:

Conditional API Selection: Automatically select the best-suited API for a task, such as choosing NLP APIs based on task complexity, language, or cost-efficiency.
Automatic Failover: If one API encounters an error or latency, Cline can switch to an alternative, ensuring uninterrupted workflow execution.
Cost-Optimization Switching: Configure Cline to use a lower-cost API for routine tasks, enhancing cost-efficiency without manual intervention.
Adding this dynamic API switch would make Cline’s workflows highly adaptable, cost-efficient, and resilient to API changes, providing users with the flexibility they need for more complex projects.

🔧 Feature Proposal for Cline: Precompiled Workflow Packages
Problem
Building custom workflows in Cline can take time, especially for users who frequently set up similar configurations. Repeatedly configuring these from scratch also increases the risk of inconsistency and setup errors, slowing down deployment for both new and existing users.

Solution
Precompiled Workflow Packages offer ready-to-use workflow setups as Cline assets:

### Which API Provider are you using?

### What happened?

Cline currently lacks support for OpenRouter's custom routing feature, leading to inconsistent behavior when utilizing certain models. For instance, the "Qwen2.5 Coder 32B Instruct" model is served by multiple providers through OpenRouter, each offering different context window sizes:

    DeepInfra: 33k context
    Hyperbolic: 128k context
    Fireworks: 33k context

Due to OpenRouter's dynamic load balancing across these providers, users experience variability in model performance, particularly concerning context handling. Implementing support for OpenRouter's custom routing within Cline would allow users to specify their preferred provider, such as Hyperbolic, to ensure consistent behavior and optimal utilization of the model's capabilities.

### Steps to reproduce

body:
### What happened?

I am experiencing an issue where the saoudrizwan.claude-dev extension in VS Code is not connecting to a locally running mcp-gsuite server. I have followed the instructions in the mcp-gsuite README to set up the server and obtain a refresh token.

### Steps to reproduce

Steps I have taken:

Created a Google Cloud project and enabled the Gmail API and Calendar API.
Configured OAuth consent screen and created OAuth 2.0 Client ID credentials.
Downloaded the credentials as credentials.json and placed it in the mcp-gsuite directory.
Used get-refresh-token.mjs to obtain a refresh token, which I added to cline_mcp_settings.json.
Set GSUITE_CLIENT_ID and GSUITE_CLIENT_SECRET as system environment variables in Windows.
Confirmed that the environment variables are correctly set by using echo %GSUITE_CLIENT_ID% and echo %GSUITE_CLIENT_SECRET% in the Command Prompt.
Started the gsuite-server.mjs using node gsuite-server.mjs.
Confirmed that the server is running and can be accessed using curl http://localhost:3000/listGmailMessages, which returns a valid JSON response.
Tried to use the listGmailMessages and listCalendarEvents tools within the saoudrizwan.claude-dev extension in VS Code.

### Relevant API REQUEST output

_No response_

### Additional context

Expected behavior:

The saoudrizwan.claude-dev extension should connect to the mcp-gsuite server and successfully execute the listGmailMessages and listCalendarEvents tools.

Actual behavior:

The extension is not connecting to the server. When I try to use the tools, I get the error message: "MCP error -2: Request timed out". The server logs show that the server is not receiving any requests from the extension.

Additional information:

The gsuite-server.mjs logs show that the server is picking up the correct GSUITE_CLIENT_ID and GSUITE_CLIENT_SECRET values from the system environment variables.
The curl tests confirm that the server is working independently and can communicate with the Gmail API.
The issue seems to be specific to the saoudrizwan.claude-dev extension.
I have examined the extension settings in VS Code, but there are no settings related to configuring local MCP servers.
I have enabled debug mode in the extension settings, but I haven't been able to find any relevant logs in the VS Code "Output" panel.
Questions for the developer:

Does the saoudrizwan.claude-dev extension support connecting to local MCP servers like mcp-gsuite?
If so, how can I configure the extension to connect to a server running on localhost:3000?
How does the extension handle environment variables for MCP servers?
Is there a way to enable more detailed logging for debugging connection issues?
Is there a recommended way to use local services or tools with the extension, even if it doesn't directly support MCP?
Does the extension have any mechanisms for defining custom actions or commands that could potentially be used to interact with a local server?
Are there any plans to add support for local MCP servers in the future?

title: Screenshot quality degradation affects visual analysis accuracy
body:
### What happened? When capturing screenshots during browser sessions, Cline is using WebP format with default compression settings, which introduces quality loss. This affects the accuracy of visual analysis in two ways: 1. False Positives: Compression artifacts are misinterpreted as visual defects, causing Cline to report errors in elements that are actually correct. 2. False Negatives: Real visual defects are masked by compression artifacts, causing Cline to miss actual issues that should be detected. The issue is particularly noticeable with: - Fine text (< 12px) - Sharp edges and 1px lines - Gradient transitions - Color accuracy checks ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a test page with precise visual elements: ```html
Small text for quality testing
``` 2. Run Cline analysis: ```typescript const result = await cline.analyzeVisual('test.html'); console.log(result.issues); ``` 3. Compare with direct browser screenshot: - Open test.html in Chrome - Take screenshot manually - Notice quality difference in: * 1px line (appears blurry in Cline) * Gradient (shows banding in Cline) * Small text (less readable in Cline) ### Relevant API REQUEST output ```shell // Current implementation in BrowserSession.ts let screenshotBase64 = await this.page.screenshot({ ...options, type: "webp", // Uses lossy compression by default }); // Console output shows compression artifacts: [Error] Visual analysis failed: - Element
appears blurred (actual: sharp) - Gradient shows banding artifacts - Text element
fails clarity check ``` ### Additional context - Issue affects all screenshot captures - Reproducible across different browsers and platforms - Impact increases with: * More complex visual elements * Finer details in UI * Color-sensitive components * Text-heavy interfaces **Environment:** - Cline Version: 3.0.4 - Puppeteer Version: ^23.4.0 - Node.js Version: 18.x - OS: Arch Linux **Proposed Solution:** Use PNG as primary format for lossless quality, with high-quality WebP as fallback only when needed. This ensures: - No compression artifacts - Accurate visual analysis - Reliable test results ![Screenshot from 2024-12-22 14-40-11](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/384c16ac-b785-4ca5-9964-04a67932f2bc) ![Cline hallucinates what he sees in the browser, then when I give him the image he sees clearly Guessing there's image compression happening in his browser - Screenshot from 2024-12-22 14-42-52](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a0712706-2e46-4356-b99a-152f59e2e835) -- FYI, this is my first contribution to this project. I asked Cline to help write this, after reviewing only CONTRIBUTING.md. Then I asked Cline to review CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, and zero changes were required: Cline writes positively by default. Thank you so much for this wonderful creation.

title: Cline panel disappears randomly
body: ### What happened? Cline was previously working fine but now it randomly goes blank. Hiding and revealing the Cline panel has no effect, but restarting Vscode fixes it. (at least temporarily) It might be related to the Github codespace disconnecting and reconnecting, but it's difficult to be sure. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use Cline as normal 2. The Cline panel goes blank 3. ### Relevant API REQUEST output _No response_ ### Operating System MacOS Sonoma but connected to a Github Codespace (Ubuntu) ### Cline Version v3.0.7 ### Additional context _No response_
